Class MusicPlayerWidget

java.lang.Object
javafx.scene.Node
javafx.scene.Parent
javafx.scene.layout.Region
javafx.scene.layout.Pane
javafx.scene.layout.HBox
view.widgets.MusicPlayerWidget
All Implemented Interfaces:
javafx.css.Styleable, javafx.event.EventTarget
public class MusicPlayerWidget extends javafx.scene.layout.HBox
Compact music-control widget displayed in the application top bar.

It renders as a single musical-note button (♪). Clicking the button toggles a floating Popup panel that shows the currently playing track name and exposes ⏮ / ⏯ / ⏭ transport controls together with a click-or-drag volume bar.

The widget wires itself to MusicManager.setOnTrackChange(Runnable) so the track label and pause/play icon are kept in sync automatically whenever the manager advances to a new track or the user pauses playback from another call site.

  • Field Details

    • mm

      private final MusicManager mm
      Shared singleton that owns all audio playback state. All transport actions delegate to this instance.

    • popup

      private final javafx.stage.Popup popup
      Floating panel that appears below the icon button when the user clicks it. Auto-hides when the user clicks outside it or presses Escape.

    • pauseBtn

      private final javafx.scene.control.Button pauseBtn
      The ⏸/▶ button inside the popup panel whose icon reflects the current pause state. Updated by refreshUI().

    • trackLabel

      private final javafx.scene.control.Label trackLabel
      Label inside the popup panel that shows the display name of the track currently playing, or "—" when nothing is loaded.

    • volBar

      private final javafx.scene.control.ProgressBar volBar
      Visual volume indicator inside the popup. Its progress property maps linearly to the [0.0, 1.0] volume range accepted by MusicManager.setVolume(double).

    • popupVisible

  • Constructor Details

    • MusicPlayerWidget

      public MusicPlayerWidget()
      Constructs the widget, adds the ♪ icon button to its layout, registers the track-change callback on MusicManager, and builds the popup panel.

      The constructor sets an initial spacing of 100 px (inherited from HBox) so that the icon button is vertically centred and does not collapse the widget to zero width when used inside a toolbar with HBox.setHgrow.

  • Method Details

    • buildPopup

      private void buildPopup()
      Constructs and configures the floating popup panel with its child controls: the "Now Playing" title, the track-name label, the ⏮ ⏯ ⏭ control row, and the volume bar. Called once from the constructor.

    • setVolume

      private void setVolume(double raw)
      Clamps the given raw value to [0.0, 1.0], updates both the volBar progress indicator and the MusicManager volume.
      Parameters:
      raw - the unclamped volume value derived from a mouse-event x-coordinate divided by the bar width; may be negative or greater than 1.0

    • togglePopup

      private void togglePopup(javafx.scene.control.Button anchor)
      Shows or hides the popup relative to the given anchor button.

      When showing, the popup is positioned just below the button's bottom edge (+ 4 px gap) aligned to its left edge. If the screen bounds of the anchor cannot be determined (e.g. the button is not yet on screen), the popup is not shown and popupVisible is left unchanged.

      Parameters:
      anchor - the ♪ icon button used as the positioning reference

    • refreshUI

      private void refreshUI()
      Synchronises all dynamic UI elements with the current state reported by MusicManager:
      • trackLabel — set to the current track name, or "—" if none
      • pauseBtn — toggled between ⏸ and ▶ based on MusicManager.isPaused()
      • volBar — re-applies the current progress value to MusicManager so the audio level stays consistent with the visual bar after a track change

      Always called on the JavaFX Application Thread, either directly or via Platform.runLater(Runnable) from the track-change callback.
